title: D. Stas and the Queue at the Buffet

legend: During a break in the buffet of the scientific lyceum of the Kingdom of Kremland, there was formed a queue of n%%ZSMJ0%% high school students numbered from 1%%ZSMJ1%% to n%%ZSMJ2%%. Initially, each student i%%ZSMJ3%% is on position i%%ZSMJ4%%. Each student i%%ZSMJ5%% is characterized by two numbers — ai%%ZSMJ6%% and bi%%ZSMJ7%%. Dissatisfaction of the person i%%ZSMJ8%% equals the product of ai%%ZSMJ9%% by the number of people standing to the left of his position, add the product bi%%ZSMJ10%% by the number of people standing to the right of his position. Formally, the dissatisfaction of the student i%%ZSMJ11%%, which is on the position j%%ZSMJ12%%, equals ai⋅(j−1)+bi⋅(n−j)%%ZSMJ13%%.
The director entrusted Stas with the task: rearrange the people in the queue so that minimize the total dissatisfaction.
Although Stas is able to solve such problems, this was not given to him. He turned for help to you.
input: The first line contains a single integer n%%ZSMJ14%% (1≤n≤105%%ZSMJ15%%) — the number of people in the queue.

Each of the following n%%ZSMJ16%% lines contains two integers ai%%ZSMJ17%% and bi%%ZSMJ18%% (1≤ai,bi≤108%%ZSMJ19%%) — the characteristic of the student i%%ZSMJ20%%, initially on the position i%%ZSMJ21%%.
output: Output one integer — minimum total dissatisfaction which can be achieved by rearranging people in the queue.
note: In the first example it is optimal to put people in this order: (3,1,2%%ZSMJ22%%). The first person is in the position of 2%%ZSMJ23%%, then his dissatisfaction will be equal to 4⋅1+2⋅1=6%%ZSMJ24%%. The second person is in the position of 3%%ZSMJ25%%, his dissatisfaction will be equal to 2⋅2+3⋅0=4%%ZSMJ26%%. The third person is in the position of 1%%ZSMJ27%%, his dissatisfaction will be equal to 6⋅0+1⋅2=2%%ZSMJ28%%. The total dissatisfaction will be 12%%ZSMJ29%%.
In the second example, you need to put people in this order: (3,2,4,1%%ZSMJ30%%). The total dissatisfaction will be 25%%ZSMJ31%%.
